evidence: # 1. bipartition; the solution colors the conflict graph and relies on the phase-parity guarantee
affordance_in_statement: A hardware conflict between two relays can only ever occur if the absolute difference between their phase frequencies is an odd number. Two relays whose phase frequencies differ by an even number will never conflict. ... the conflict list is guaranteed to adhere to this strict rule.
removal_suggestion: Replace the odd-difference rule with an even-difference rule and invert the following sentence, so odd cycles are allowed and the conflict graph is no longer guaranteed to be bipartite.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the guaranteed parity structure to bipartition the conflict graph and construct the answer from the color classes instead of solving a general independent-set problem.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: A hardware conflict ... can only ever occur if the absolute difference between their phase frequencies is an odd number.

common_affordance: The conflict graph is guaranteed to be bipartite because conflicts can occur only between relays of opposite phase parity.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It treated a bipartition, typically one color class, as sufficient for the requested answer and did not correctly handle cases where a larger independent set requires vertices from both sides.
It made the same incorrect reduction from maximum independent set to selecting a color class, so it can reject valid independent sets assembled from both bipartition sides.
It relied on bipartite coloring and color-class selection rather than computing whether the maximum independent set has size at least k.

recommended_edit: Change the phase rule so conflicts are possible only when the phase-frequency difference is even, and state that odd differences never conflict. This preserves the scenario and formats while permitting odd cycles, defeating the bipartition shortcut.
